research.title: Exploring BNB Chain NewL1
research.subtitle: Orderveil starts from NewL1's public TEE Gateway proposal and turns its ordering rules into experiments anyone can run, inspect and replay.
research.relationTitle: How Orderveil relates to the proposal

relation.text: Implements the proposal's public ordering rules as a deterministic JavaScript engine: fee-rate ordering, H(txHash‖salt) ties, 5-tick opt-in delay, after-ref only.
Records SubBlock fields, input commitments and payload hashes so every experiment can be replayed and verified.
Does not run a TEE, produce attestation or an enclaveSig, or connect to NewL1. Those are proposal-level features this site only describes.
Fills gaps the proposal leaves open (salt derivation, hashing, refund share) with clearly labelled Orderveil choices.

topology.ariaLabel: Interactive network topology of the simulated gateway

walletA.label: Wallet A
walletA.desc: Represents the user whose swap is being studied. In the simulation it submits exactly one transaction (transactionId “user”).

walletB.label: Wallet B
walletB.desc: Represents other users. The simulation generates their swaps deterministically from the seed (size, direction, fee rate, arrival tick).

walletC.label: Wallet C
walletC.desc: Represents MEV actors: a sandwich attacker on the public path, a blind or hint-informed trader on gateway paths, and backrun searchers on the opt-in path.

ingress.label: Encrypted Ingress
ingress.desc: In the proposal, transactions are decrypted only inside the TEE. Orderveil models the information boundary (who can see what) but does not encrypt anything; there is no TEE.

classifier.label: Transaction Classifier
classifier.desc: Routes each transaction to the protected path (default) or the opt-in delayed path. Only opt-in transactions produce a hint and a targetCommitment.

protectedQueue.label: Protected Queue
protectedQueue.desc: Default path. Contents are never disclosed to simulated searchers and cannot be referenced by bundles. A transaction enters its arrival tick.

optinQueue.label: Opt-in Queue
optinQueue.desc: User-authorized path. The unsigned transaction body is published as a hint and inclusion is delayed by 5 ticks (≈100 ms logical) so searchers can submit after-ref backruns.

ordering.label: Deterministic Ordering Engine
ordering.desc: Orders each tick's frozen set by effective fee rate (descending), breaks ties with SHA-256(txHash‖salt), keeps sender nonce order and places the best after-ref bundle directly after its target.

subblock.label: SubBlock Generator
subblock.desc: Binds each tick's output to gatewayId, workloadId, rulesetVersion, term, slot, tick, parentSubBlockHash, inputCommitment and payloadHash. No enclaveSig is produced because there is no TEE.

packaging.label: Block Packaging
packaging.desc: Concatenates SubBlocks in acknowledged order into the final sequence that the AMM executes. Transactions cannot be removed, inserted or reordered.

validator.label: Validator
validator.desc: In the proposal, the validator verifies, signs and proposes. Here it is conceptual: the simulation executes the packaged order and reports outcomes; no consensus is simulated.

settlementContract.label: Commitment Contract
settlementContract.desc: OrderveilCommitments on BSC Testnet. From the Playground's Audit tab you can publish an experiment's record digest, final SubBlock hash and execution hash here with your wallet. It records that the commitment existed; it does not settle trades.

bscTestnet.label: BSC Testnet
bscTestnet.desc: Connected for audit commitments only (chain ID 97). Experiment transactions are never sent to BSC, and BSC's ordering is not affected by Orderveil.

compare.caveatTitle: Read these results with the model in mind
caveats: Outcomes depend on the seed, sizes and fee rates you chose. Protected ordering does not guarantee a better price.
On the protected path the adversary cannot see your trade, but a blind high-fee trade in the same direction can still coincidentally hurt you (proposal §05 residual risk).
The public path assumes a perfectly informed attacker that wins fee priority; real attackers face competition, latency and failure.
MEV-related loss is measured against the same run without the adversary, so normal price impact from other users is not counted as MEV.

audit.importText: Load an exported record. Orderveil re-derives the inputs from the parameters and seed, re-runs ordering and AMM execution, and compares every commitment — it does not just compare stored fields.
audit.invalidJson: The file is not valid JSON.
audit.fromCurrent: Source: current experiment (exported and re-imported in memory)
audit.note: createdAt is informational and excluded from all hashes. The simulationSignature uses a fresh local ed25519 key per export; it shows the record wasn't altered after export, and nothing more. It is not a TEE attestation or an enclaveSig.

common: Constant-product pool (x·y=k) with an input-side fee that stays in the pool; integer math in 18-decimal units, outputs rounded down.
External reference price is fixed at the initial pool price; P&L is valued at that price.
Gas cost = gas units × effective fee rate, paid in BNB. Gas units are a simulation assumption, not measured data.
Other order flow is generated deterministically from the seed. Same seed and inputs reproduce the same experiment.
Ticks are logical time. 20 ms is the proposal's engineering target, not a latency this website or any chain achieved.
public: The attacker sees your pending transaction, bids a higher fee for the front-run and a slightly lower fee for the back-run.
Background transactions with fees between the two legs can land inside the sandwich, exactly as fee ordering dictates.
If the front-run pushes you past your slippage limit, your transaction reverts and the attacker unwinds at a loss.
protected: The adversary cannot observe your transaction (no hints, no after-ref). It can only submit a blind high-fee trade in the same tick.
Whether the blind guess matches your direction comes from the seed or the option you choose; a match reproduces the proposal's stated residual risk.
The blind position is closed with an ordinary transaction in the next tick, after the SubBlock is published.
optin: Your unsigned transaction body is disclosed as a hint at your arrival tick; inclusion is delayed by 5 ticks.
Searchers compute an optimal backrun on the disclosed pool state and commit a tip; the best tip is placed directly after you.

Orderveil model finding: with full-body hints, an informed trader can still enter an earlier tick through the ordinary path. Your slippage limit is the remaining protection. This is a property of this simplified model, not a claim about the final NewL1 design.
Refund share and the 75/25 split of the remainder are assumptions for illustration.

tech.title: Exploring the BNB Chain NewL1 vision
tech.subtitle: What NewL1's TEE Gateway proposes, why transaction ordering matters, and exactly which parts Orderveil implements as a simulation.

newl1.title: What is NewL1?
body: NewL1 is described by BNB Chain as a vertical-optimized general-purpose L1: a new, fully EVM-compatible member of the BNB Chain family built for trading, payments, privacy and AI.

It complements BSC rather than replacing it, connected through an official native bridge. BNB is the native token, and no new token will be issued for NewL1. ORVL, the reserved ticker of this independent project, is unrelated to BNB Chain or NewL1.
newl1.orderveil: context only — nothing here connects to NewL1

whyOrdering.title: Why transaction ordering matters
body: When the content of a transaction is visible before it is ordered, whoever controls or can influence ordering can trade around it: buy before a large buy and sell right after. The victim receives fewer tokens; the difference becomes MEV.

The proposal's goals table states the response: privacy (hidden before ordering), fairness (public, replayable rules where the same frozen input set, ruleset version and random salt produce the same order), and internalizing beneficial MEV only when users authorize disclosure.
whyOrdering.orderveil: the Playground measures this loss with real AMM math

architecture.title: TEE Gateway architecture
body: The Gateway is proposed as an attestable ordering and packaging service, not a new consensus role. It receives transactions inside a VM-based TEE (TDX first, SEV-SNP as an alternative backend), applies public rules, generates a continuous SubBlock stream, and produces the final block package at the end of the slot. The validator verifies, signs and proposes.
Each validator selects a primary and a standby Gateway in the same region. Only the primary streams during normal operation; failover happens at an explicit tick boundary.
architecture.orderveil: the components are simulated as pure functions; no TEE, no network

protected.title: Protected order flow
body: Transactions are private by default: before ordering, operators, validators and searchers see only ciphertext, and bundles cannot reference protected transactions. A protected transaction receives no hint and enters the next available tick.

The proposal is explicit about residual risk: frontrunning and sandwiching are prohibited structurally, yet a blindly submitted, high-fee front leg may coincidentally succeed. Orderveil models exactly that case instead of claiming zero MEV.

deterministic.title: Deterministic ordering and 20 ms ticks
body: Ordering happens per tick over a frozen input set. In the General segment transactions are sorted by effective fee rate, and ties are broken by H(txHash ‖ salt). The tick length is an engineering target of 20 ms, to be validated at P50/P99 on real TEE, networking and storage.

Orderveil fixes the parts the proposal leaves open in a versioned ruleset: SHA-256 as H, ascending byte order for ties, a salt derived from the seed, parent SubBlock hash and tick, and preserved per-sender nonce order. Changing any of them changes the ruleset version.
deterministic.orderveil: pure JS engine with tests for reproducibility

backruns.title: Opt-in disclosure and after-ref backruns
body: Users can authorize disclosure. The default hint is the complete unsigned transaction body, published simultaneously to all subscribers, while the signature stays inside the TEE. Inclusion is delayed by 5 ticks, giving searchers about 100 ms to simulate and submit.

Searchers reference the target through a Gateway-generated targetCommitment and may only be placed immediately after it (after-ref). There is no before-ref. Candidates compete on committed tips, and the value can be returned to order flow.
backruns.orderveil: hint stream, commitments, validity checks and tip competition

subblocks.title: SubBlock streaming
body: Every SubBlock binds at least gatewayId, workloadId, rulesetVersion, term, slot, tick, parentSubBlockHash, inputCommitment, payloadHash and enclaveSig. The final package may concatenate SubBlocks only in acknowledged order.
Orderveil produces all of these fields except enclaveSig, which only a real TEE can produce. Experiment records carry a separate local simulationSignature that is never presented as TEE proof.
subblocks.orderveil: one SubBlock per logical tick, chained by parent hash

auditing.title: Replayable auditing
body: The proposal keeps three public facts: allowed workloads, the enclave key each Gateway uses this epoch, and which ordering inputs and rules produced the final block. Deterministic replay recomputes input commitments, rulesets, payloadHash and salt-dependent results to detect ordering violations or fabricated outputs.

Orderveil's replay tool re-derives inputs from the recorded parameters, re-runs ordering and AMM execution, and compares every commitment. Tampering with a transaction, the salt, the ordering result or an input commitment makes replay fail.
auditing.orderveil: export → import → replay in the Playground

arch.caption: Simplified from the proposal's §03 architecture and §3.1 component table. enclaveSig is produced only by a real TEE and is absent from Orderveil.

ticks.caption: Logical timeline. A protected transaction arriving in tick 1 is ordered in tick 1. An opt-in transaction arriving in tick 1 is disclosed immediately and included in tick 6; backruns submitted during ticks 2–5 are placed right after it.

mapping.title: NewL1 technology mapping
mapping.subtitle: Each NewL1 concept, the proposal's description, and what Orderveil actually implements today. “Planned” is never written as “implemented”.

teeGateway.official: Attestable ordering and packaging service in a VM-based TEE, primary + standby per validator.
teeGateway.impl: Gateway architecture simulation: ingress, classifier, ordering, SubBlocks, packaging as pure functions.
teeGateway.assumptions: Single gateway, single term and slot, no failover, no network.
teeGateway.missing: TEE execution, RA-TLS, standby sync, failover, encrypted WAL.

privateDefault.official: Protected transactions stay hidden from operators, validators and searchers before ordering.
privateDefault.impl: Protected order flow: no hint, no commitment, cannot be referenced; tests check searcher views for leaks.
privateDefault.assumptions: Privacy is an information boundary in code, not encryption.

deterministic.official: Sort by effective fee rate; break ties using H(txHash ‖ salt).
deterministic.impl: JavaScript ordering engine with a versioned ruleset and reproducibility tests.
deterministic.assumptions: H = SHA-256; ties ascending; nonce order preserved; lanes and guaranteed-inclusion tail omitted.
deterministic.missing: Lane segments, atomic multi-tx user bundles beyond backruns, guaranteed-inclusion tail.

tick.official: Engineering target; validate P50/P99 on real hardware.
tick.impl: Logical tick simulator with tick index, frozen set, ordering and output batch.
tick.assumptions: Logical time only; nothing is timed.

optin.official: Authorize the unsigned body (or a summary) as a hint; default delay 5 ticks.
optin.impl: Authorized hint model with targetCommitment and a 5-tick window.
optin.assumptions: Full-body hints only; searchers value the target on the state at disclosure.
optin.missing: Field-level summaries, D-lagged execution state, gw_* RPC interfaces.

afterRef.official: Only immediately after the target; no before-ref; compete on committed tips.
afterRef.impl: Backrun ordering experiment with validity checks, tip competition and atomic exclusion.
afterRef.assumptions: One backrun per target; a backrun is excluded if its target or itself reverts.

subblock.official: Each SubBlock binds slot, tick, parent hash, commitments and enclaveSig.
subblock.impl: SubBlock visualization with all fields except enclaveSig.
subblock.assumptions: SHA-256 over canonical JSON; empty ticks still emit SubBlocks.
subblock.missing: enclaveSig, validator ACKs, block package proof summary.

inputCommitment.impl: Reproducible audit records with input commitment, payload hash and ruleset version per tick.
inputCommitment.assumptions: Commitment = SHA-256 over sorted hashes with domain separation.

replay.official: Recompute commitments, rulesets, payloadHash and salt-dependent results.
replay.impl: Replay verification tool: export, import, re-run, compare; Replay Passed / Failed.
replay.assumptions: Records are self-contained JSON with a local integrity signature.
replay.missing: Cross-platform test vectors against a real gateway.

attestation.official: Quotes bind short-lived enclave keys to allowed workloads; per-tick compact signatures.
attestation.impl: Not implemented. Orderveil never labels its signature as attestation.
attestation.missing: Everything: TDX/SEV-SNP quotes, workload measurements, key rotation.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.lead: Orderveil Gateway Lab is a research platform for protected transaction ordering and MEV. Version 1 runs entirely in your browser.

blocks.text: The project starts from BNB Chain NewL1's public TEE Gateway proposal and turns its ordering rules into experiments: a deterministic ordering engine, a logical tick and SubBlock simulator, a constant-product AMM with an adversary, and an audit record that anyone can replay.
Three kinds of results

head: Kind
Meaning
In v1
rows: Local mathematical model and ordering experiment
Real testnet transactions and contract checks
Optional: publish an experiment's commitment to BSC Testnet from the Audit tab
Actually connected to and verified on NewL1

newl1-research.title: NewL1 Research
newl1-research.lead: The official sources Orderveil is built on, read on 2026-10-20.

blocks.text: Key points used by Orderveil

items: Core proposal: the Gateway is an attestable ordering and packaging service, not a new consensus role; the validator retains final signing authority.
Private by default; MEV exposed only within user-authorized boundaries.
Protected path: no hints, no after-ref references, enter the next available tick.
Opt-in delayed path: unsigned body or summary as hint, default delay 5 ticks (≈100 ms).
General ordering: effective fee rate; ties by H(txHash ‖ salt).
After-ref: only immediately after the target; no before-ref; compete on committed tips.
SubBlocks bind gatewayId, workloadId, rulesetVersion, term, slot, tick, parentSubBlockHash, inputCommitment, payloadHash, enclaveSig.
Replay data: frozen-set commitments, rule parameters, random salt, final order.
Residual risk acknowledged: a blindly submitted high-fee front leg may coincidentally succeed.

blocks.text: Details the proposal does not specify

Hash function for H, byte encoding, salt source, refund share and candidate scoring beyond committed tips are not defined in the public text. Orderveil fills them with explicit, versioned simulation choices and never presents them as protocol facts. See docs/NEWL1_RESEARCH.md in the repository for the full section-by-section mapping.

simulation-model.title: Simulation Model
simulation-model.lead: How a Playground experiment is constructed. Every value is derived from the inputs and the seed.

blocks.text: Actors

items: User — one swap, arrival tick 1, minimum output from the slippage tolerance applied to a quote on the initial pool.
Other order flow — N swaps whose direction, size (0.05–0.5% of the input reserve), fee rate (0.5–2.5 gwei) and arrival tick (0–7) come from SHA-256 draws on the seed.
Adversary — depends on the mode (below).
Searchers — opt-in only; each computes the optimal backrun and commits a seeded share (30–90%) of the expected net profit as a tip.

blocks.text: Modes

head: Mode
Visibility
Adversary behaviour
rows: Everything visible; one block ordered by fee
Front-run at a higher fee, back-run at a slightly lower fee, sells the full position
Blind high-fee trade in the same tick, direction guessed; exits next tick
Unsigned body disclosed at arrival; inclusion after 5 ticks
Hint-informed ordinary trade in an earlier tick; searchers compete for the after-ref slot

blocks.text: Measuring MEV-related loss

Each mode is run twice: as configured, and with the adversary removed. MEV-related loss is the difference in your output between the two runs, valued at the reference price. Price impact caused by other users therefore isn't counted as MEV. A negative value means the adversary's trade happened to improve your price.

Defaults are examples chosen to make each effect visible. A different seed can make the protected path look worse than the public one. That is a property of the model, and the reason the site never claims guaranteed protection.

amm-math.title: AMM Mathematics
amm-math.lead: Uniswap-V2-style constant product with an input-side fee, computed in 18-decimal integers.

blocks.text:
x · y = k
effectiveIn = amountIn · (10000 − feeBps) / 10000
amountOut   = reserveOut · effectiveIn / (reserveIn + effectiveIn)      (floor)
reserveIn'  = reserveIn + amountIn          # fee stays in the pool, k grows
reserveOut' = reserveOut − amountOut
Amounts are BigInt in the smallest unit; nothing depends on floating-point. Conversions to decimals happen only for display and charts.
Slippage and failure

minOut = quote(initialPool, amountIn) · (10000 − slippageBps) / 10000
if amountOut < minOut → reverted, pool unchanged, gas still paid
Optimal backrun (opt-in searchers)

reference price P = Rq0 / Rb0,  g = 1 − fee
pool overpriced:  x* = (√(g·Rb·Rq / P) − Rb) / g      sell BASE
pool underpriced: y* = (√(g·Rb·Rq·P) − Rq) / g      buy BASE with QUOTE
Profit accounting

items: Gross trading P&L = change in token balances valued at the reference price (AMM fees are already inside it).
AMM fees paid are reported separately for transparency.
Gas = gas units × effective fee rate (BNB), converted at the reference price.
Net = gross − gas (− committed tip for searchers).

ordering-rules.title: Ordering Rules
ordering-rules.lead: Ruleset orderveil-sim/ruleset/0.1.0. Any behavioural change bumps the version.

head: Rule
Definition
Origin
rows: Logical 20 ms; tick t covers [20t, 20t+20) ms
Immediately after target; best committedTip; ties SHA-256(bundleHash ‖ salt); max 1 per target

blocks.text: Bundle validity checks (in order)

items: beforeRef present → rejected_before_ref
no afterRef → rejected_no_target
afterRef is a protected tx hash or its derived commitment → rejected_protected_target
afterRef matches no published hint → rejected_unknown_target
no member transactions → rejected_empty
arrived before the hint was disclosed → rejected_before_disclosure
arrived at or after the target's inclusion tick → rejected_late
validity window doesn't cover the inclusion tick → rejected_validity_window
committedTip below floor → rejected_tip_floor
at execution: target or member reverted → whole bundle excluded

audit-records.title: Audit Records
audit-records.lead: Every experiment can be exported as a self-contained JSON record and replayed by anyone.

blocks.text: Record contents

items: schema: orderveil.experiment/v1, classification: simulation
experimentId = first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over ruleset version, parameters and inputs
ruleset: the full parameter object
config.params: normalized parameters including seed
inputs: every transaction and bundle with its content hash
outputs: per-tick salt, frozen set, ordered entries, inputCommitment, payloadHash, parent and SubBlock hash; final order; AMM execution with executionHash
simulationSignature: ed25519 over the record digest with a fresh local key

blocks.text: Canonical hashing

canonical JSON = sorted keys, no whitespace, BigInt → decimal string
txHash          = SHA-256(canonical({domain:"ORVL/tx/v1", …body}))
inputCommitment = SHA-256("ORVL/input/v1|" ‖ u64(tick) ‖ u64(n) ‖ sorted txHashes ‖ "|bundles|" ‖ u64(m) ‖ sorted bundleHashes)
payloadHash     = SHA-256(canonical({domain:"ORVL/payload/v1", entries}))
subBlockHash    = SHA-256(canonical({domain:"ORVL/subblock/v1", …header}))
What replay checks

Replay recomputes rather than compares. It verifies every content hash, regenerates the inputs from the parameters and seed, re-runs the ordering engine and the AMM, and compares each tick's salt, frozen set, input commitment, ordering, payload hash and SubBlock chain, plus bundle decisions, hints, final order and execution. Finally it verifies the local signature. Tampering with a transaction, the salt, the seed, the ordering or a commitment fails replay.
createdAt is informational and excluded from all hashes. The simulationSignature only shows the record wasn't modified after export. It is not a TEE attestation and not an enclaveSig.
On-chain commitments (BSC Testnet)

From the Audit tab, a connected wallet can call OrderveilCommitments.commit(recordDigest, experimentId, finalSubBlockHash, executionHash, rulesetVersion) on BSC Testnet. Each digest can be committed once. Anyone who imports a record can read its commitment without a wallet: replay recomputes the digest, then the site checks that the on-chain fields match the record.
A commitment proves the record existed no later than its block. It is a Testnet Experiment artifact: it does not mean BSC ordering is controlled by Orderveil, and it is not a NewL1 or TEE proof.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.lead: What this version does not do, stated plainly.

items: No TEE, no attestation, no enclaveSig, no RA-TLS. Privacy is an information boundary in code, not encryption.
No connection to NewL1. BSC Testnet is used only to store optional audit commitments; experiment transactions are never sent to any chain.
Ticks are logical; 20 ms is the proposal's target, not a measured latency.
Single pool, single gateway, single slot. No lanes, no guaranteed-inclusion tail, no failover.
Searchers value backruns on the pool state at disclosure, not on D-lagged executed state.
The external price is fixed at the initial pool price; there is no CEX price process.
Attackers follow fixed strategies; there is no strategic competition between multiple attackers.
The opt-in “informed front leg” finding comes from this simplified model and its full-body hints. The proposal also allows field-level summaries and further policy that may change the outcome.
Gas units and refund shares are assumptions.
Results are model outputs. They do not predict real-world MEV and are not financial advice.

Token
Orderveil (ORVL) is a reserved name for a possible future project token. Nothing is deployed, sold or distributed, there is no tokenomics, and it has no relation to BNB, BNB Chain or NewL1.

wallet.disclaimer: Orderveil only asks your wallet to sign BSC Testnet transactions that you start yourself (audit commitments). It never requests mainnet funds or message signatures.
